tagline.text: A quiet white-sand resort island in the sea off northern Iloilo

location.label: Location
location.text: Off the coast of Carles, Iloilo Province

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱15,000–30,000 (per person, 2 nights 3 days including flights)

children.text: Sicogon is an island of about 11.6 square kilometers in the Visayan Sea, northeast of Panay, with a long white-sand beach, coconut palms and 214 m Mt. Opao. It is a quiet getaway reachable by direct charter flight from Manila or by boat from Estancia port.
Sicogon Island belongs to the municipality of Carles in northern Iloilo Province and lies in the Visayan Sea about
10km

off the northeast coast of Panay. Its total area is about 11.6 square kilometers, and roughly 4,275 people (2020 census) live in its three barangays: Alipata, Buaya and San Fernando. The highest point is Mt. Opao,
tall, northeast of Barangay Buaya.

The island became widely known in the 1970s. It was already popular as a film location and tourist spot then, and in 1976 President Marcos designated it a tourist zone. Development stalled in the 1980s, travelers moved on to other islands such as Boracay, and Sicogon stayed a quiet fishing community for a long time. In 2013 Typhoon Haiyan passed over the island and damaged fishing boats and nets.

Today Sicogon is a planned resort island managed by Sicogon Island Tourism Estate Corp. (SITEC), a joint venture of Ayala Land and Sicogon Development Corp. (SIDECO). A development plan worth about ₱10 billion was announced in 2013. The first luxury stay, Balay Kogon, opened in December 2016, the 52-room Huni Sicogon in May 2018, and the bungalow-style Hatch Sicogon in 2023. The island has its own airport and jetty port, so getting in is fairly easy.
If you expect a lively beach like Boracay, this is not it. On the roughly
5km

of San Fernando and Buaya beaches there is no shopping strip and no clubs; you have kayaking and paddleboarding by day and sandbar walks at sunset. In the forest at the heart of the island you will find the Mt. Opao trail and the Lagoon Eco-Trail, and you can make a day trip to Islas de Gigantes, about an hour away by boat. It suits travelers who want to relax and add one island tour.
A white-sand beach of about
5km
runs along the island, lined with coconut palms and clear water. At low tide shallow sandbars appear, perfect for a sunset walk. You can kayak, paddleboard and play beach volleyball.
The island's highest peak,
tall, takes about
1.5 to 2 hours

to climb on foot. From the summit you can see the airport, the resort, nearby islands and the coast of mainland Panay. Visitors report seeing wild pitcher plants and tasting wild batwan and kamias fruit in the forest.

This easy forest path opened relatively recently and is described as a place to spot birds and the Visayan warty pig. It suits families who find Mt. Opao too demanding. Check with your resort in advance whether it is open.
It is about
1 hour

by banca from the Sicogon jetty. The tour covers the cliff-ringed saltwater lagoon of Tangke Island, the cliffs of Cabugao Island, the rock formations of Antonia Island and the Bantigue sandbar, and includes fresh scallops.
Kiteboarding lessons are available at Hatch Sicogon. Go when the wind is blowing; other options include kayaking, paddleboarding, snorkeling and pontoon rides.
The small island of Tumaguin beside Sicogon is said to be reachable on foot at low tide. It is close to Balay Kogon and a starting point for island hopping. Always check the tide before crossing.

Restaurants on the island serve scallops grilled, baked with butter and cheese, or as adobo. Fresh scallops eaten on the boat during the tour are a highlight. There is also a crispy scallop snack you can take home.

items.title: 2 nights 3 days relaxing course
items.subtitle: Fly in and take it slow on the island

children.text: Take a morning flight from Manila and land at Sicogon Airport. The resort is about
5 minutes
away by car. Unpack and relax on the beach.
Swim and kayak at San Fernando beach. Have a drink at the pool bar during happy hour, between 4 and 6 p.m., and watch the sunset.
Start the Mt. Opao hike early. One reviewer started at
and finished at
. It is best to come down before the heat arrives.
Return to your room, have breakfast and rest, then walk toward Buaya beach and Tumaguin Island in the afternoon.
Check out and fly back to Manila on the morning flight. Luggage limits are strict, so pack light.
Many sources say the direct flight from Manila operates on Mondays and Fridays, so plan either a Friday-to-Monday long weekend or a Monday-to-Friday weekday trip.

items.title: 3 nights 4 days with an island tour
items.subtitle: A course with a Gigantes day tour

children.text: Arrive, check in and relax on the beach. In the evening try local food such as scallops and chicken binakol at the resort restaurant.
Take a banca to Islas de Gigantes early. Leaving early is the trick to avoiding the tour groups arriving from Iloilo.
Visit the saltwater lagoon on Tangke Island, Cabugao Island and the Bantigue sandbar, then have lunch and snorkel at Antonia Island.
Hike Mt. Opao or walk the Lagoon Eco-Trail, then try a kiteboarding lesson or paddleboarding in the afternoon.
Enjoy a relaxed breakfast and fly back on the morning flight.
Island tour prices are negotiated per boat; a 2023 review suggested budgeting about ₱5,000 per group for a day. Confirm again on site.
AirSWIFT flies between Manila (NAIA Terminal 4) and Sicogon Airport (ICO). As of 2023 it operated on Mondays and Fridays, and the flight time is about
55 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
depending on the source.
A January 2023 review put the round trip at about ₱9,000. Reviewers say the checked baggage limit of
10kg
and the single carry-on limit of
7kg
are strictly enforced.
For a Friday flight leaving in the early morning, travelers were told to arrive at NAIA by
. Days and times change, so check with AirSWIFT.
The resort is about 5 minutes by car from the airport.

items.title: From Iloilo City via Estancia port

children.text: A bus or van from Iloilo City to Estancia costs about ₱200 and takes about
2 to 3 hours
The boat from Estancia port to Sicogon takes about
45 minutes to 1 hour
depending on the weather and cost about ₱80 in 2023. Reviews say the public passenger boat leaves about once a day, around 1 p.m., so be sure to check the schedule locally.
One review says chartering a banca costs about ₱2,500, though this varies by time.
A bus or van from Iloilo City to Carles takes about
4 hours
and costs about ₱170–180.
The boat from Carles to the island takes about
30 minutes
and costs about ₱100 (2023 information).
You can fly from Manila to Roxas City (Capiz) and travel on to Estancia port. One source says this takes about 1 hour 30 minutes.
From Estancia port, take the boat to the island as described above.
The island's roads are narrow, so you get around by motorbike (habal-habal) rather than by car. One reviewer paid about ₱150 round trip from the resort to the trailhead.
The resort and the beach are within walking distance of each other.

The dry season from November to May is the best time to visit Sicogon. The sea is calm and the sky clear, which makes island hopping and the Mt. Opao hike easier. If kiteboarding is your goal, ask the resort when the wind blows.

June to October is the rainy season, with rain and waves that can make boats rough or cancel them. Typhoons also pass through, so leave room in your schedule and book flights and boats on refundable or changeable terms.

Most accommodation on the island is in Ayala-affiliated resorts. Huni Sicogon is a 52-room boutique resort that opened in 2018, with a free-form infinity pool, an all-day restaurant, a pool bar and a shallow white-sand beach. Balay Kogon is a 26-room boutique stay that opened in December 2016, near Buaya beach with a view deck, close enough to Tumaguin Island to make island hopping easy. Hatch Sicogon is a beach hostel-style stay that opened in 2023; solo travelers can book a bed from ₱1,250, and it has a beach bar and kiteboarding lessons.

Think of the resort restaurant as nearly the only place to eat. Prices in 2023 reviews were about ₱400 for grilled scallops, ₱570 for stuffed squid, ₱270 for chicken binakol, ₱450 for batchoy and ₱500 for breakfast. Food can take close to an hour to arrive, so order ahead. Some cocktails use batwan, a local fruit. Reviews say the resort takes cash only and the island has no ATM, so bring plenty of cash.
The direct flight runs only on set days, so book your flight first and fit the accommodation around it.
Baggage limits (checked
10kg
, carry-on
7kg
) are said to be strict, so pack light.
There is no ATM on the island, so bring plenty of cash. Reviews say the resort takes cash only.
If you climb Mt. Opao at dawn it is not hot and the views from the top are clear. Some reviewers set out around
Leave early for the Gigantes tour to avoid the crowds of tour groups.
Order meals ahead and allow at least an hour.
Bring insect repellent, sunscreen and water shoes.
When walking across to Tumaguin Island, always check the tide.
Most lodging and restaurants on the island belong to one operator, so prices are high and choices few, and boats and flights can change with the weather.
Most prices and schedules in this guide are based on 2017–2023 reviews and notices. Check the latest announcements before you book.
Public passenger boats are few, about one a day. If you miss it you must charter a banca.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons boats can be rough or cancelled, so leave slack in your schedule.
Reviews say the Mt. Opao area is a wildlife sanctuary. Do not pick plants or leave trash.
About
1 hour
away by banca. It is famous for the Tangke Island lagoon, Cabugao Island and its scallops.
A port town north of Iloilo and the departure point for public boats to Sicogon. It is not listed as a separate destination.
An island group northeast of Iloilo with Pan de Azucar Island and sandbars. It is fairly close to Sicogon but needs a separate trip.
The main city of Capiz, which can serve as a gateway to Sicogon.
The best-known beach on the same island of Panay, lively in contrast to Sicogon.
